# SpecDD

> SpecDD is an open-source framework for spec-driven development. It gives humans and AI agents the local context to
> build software that fits the project: its product intent, architecture, behavior, and boundaries.

Small, human-readable `.sdd` specs live beside the code, infrastructure, automation, or documentation they describe.
They turn project decisions into contracts that guide implementation, review, and verification. The reasoning behind
important behavior stays in the repository, ready for your next session, another agent, or a new contributor.

SpecDD works for individual developers, teams, small businesses, and large organizations, with or without AI. It is
language-agnostic and agent-agnostic: plain files in Git keep project knowledge portable across tools, editors, and models.

Use this file as a map to the [official SpecDD website](https://specdd.ai/) and project resources. Follow the linked
guides for setup, language rules, workflows, and examples.

## Why use SpecDD

A patch can look correct and still miss a requirement, cross an architectural boundary, or change behavior you meant
to preserve. The missing context often lives in notes, prompts, tickets, reviews, or memory. AI agents can repeat those
plausible mistakes across sessions, leaving you to explain the same constraints again.

SpecDD makes that context local, persistent, and reviewable. You can return to an old project, start another agent
session, or hand work to someone else with the relevant decisions already recorded. Prompts can focus on the task,
and changes can be checked against the intended behavior. The value extends across the development process:

- [Less repeated correction](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-for-developers/): give agents the project's actual rules
  before implementation, reducing the need to explain the same boundary in every prompt and review.
- [Better software design](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-superpowers-better-software-design/): naming responsibilities
  and dependencies exposes unclear ownership and overloaded modules while the design is still easy to change.
- [Safer delivery](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-superpowers-safer-delivery/): explicit scope and completion criteria
  help contain overbuilding and preserve behavior during refactoring, whether you make the change or delegate it.
- [Traceable intent](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-superpowers-traceable-intent/): connect requirements with code and
  verification so you can identify missing tests, contract violations, and drift.
- [Reusable project knowledge](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-for-non-technical-users/#what-if-i-am-the-only-member-and-i-have-no-team):
  preserve decisions for future work, whether you return after a break, switch agents, or bring someone into the project.
- [Clearer collaboration](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-as-the-interface-between-product-and-development-teams/):
  when work involves others, give product, development, QA, and support a common understanding of behavior before coding.

You can describe intended behavior in plain language and add technical detail as needed. One person can define,
implement, and verify a feature; collaborators can use the same spec when responsibilities are shared. Code implements
the behavior, specs preserve its intent, and automated tests provide evidence that the important behavior holds.

The same approach applies to infrastructure and operations, including Ansible roles, Terraform modules, and CI workflows.

Adoption can start with one area where missing context already costs time: a frequently changed service, a legacy
module, an integration, or an operational workflow. New projects can begin with specs; existing projects can
add them around active work. A maintained spec can guide many future changes, spreading the writing effort across the
work it supports.

## Start here

- [Framework reference](https://specdd.ai/reference/README.md): what SpecDD is, how the pieces fit together, and the
  development model, with examples.
- [Quickstart](https://specdd.ai/quickstart/): the shortest path from project setup to a small change guided by reviewed specs.
- [Working example](https://github.com/specdd/example): a Travel Planner project with specs, source code, tests, and agent
  entrypoints.

## Framework and language references

For work inside a SpecDD project, use its installed `.specdd/bootstrap.md`, enabled plugins, and applicable local
specs as the project instructions. The published references below explain the framework and its file format.

- [Agent bootstrap](https://specdd.ai/reference/src/.specdd/bootstrap.md): agent operating rules, spec discovery,
  inheritance, write authority, conflict handling, and verification.
- [Language reference](https://specdd.ai/language-reference/): formal `.sdd` syntax, section definitions, paths, symbols,
  task markers, parsing, and validation.
- [Technical writing style guide](https://specdd.ai/style-guide/): guidance for clear documentation, technical references,
  and agent instructions.
- [Security guide](https://specdd.ai/security/): release and plugin signatures, manual verification, and review of
  agent-facing instructions.

## Tools, integrations, and plugins

The command-line interface (CLI) manages project setup and framework updates. Editor integrations help people write
specs, and agent integrations provide skills for common SpecDD tasks. Framework plugins extend projects with reusable
instructions, document types, and workflows.

- [Tools and setup guide](https://specdd.ai/tools/): CLI installation and usage, editor support, and agent setup.
- [Dedicated agent integrations](https://specdd.ai/tools/#dedicated-agent-plugins): setup for Codex, Claude Code,
  GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Junie, and Cline.
- [Universal Agent Skills](https://specdd.ai/tools/#universal-agent-skills): portable skills for compatible clients.
- [Framework plugin guide](https://specdd.ai/plugins/): install, list, update, and publish plugins from official,
  third-party, or team repositories.
- [Domain & Solution Design (DSD)](https://specdd.ai/plugins/official/dsd/): connect business rules, architecture decisions,
  and acceptance criteria with implementation specs through Domain Definitions and Solution Designs.
- [SpecDD Style Guide (SSG)](https://specdd.ai/plugins/official/ssg/): write and review SpecDD artifacts while preserving
  their meaning and native formats.

## Find a practical guide

Browse the [how-to index](https://specdd.ai/how-to/) for the full collection, or start with the topic that matches the task:

- [Getting started](https://specdd.ai/how-to/getting-started/): choose a first use case and complete a spec-driven change.
- [Adopt SpecDD in an existing project](https://specdd.ai/how-to/adopt-specdd-on-existing-projects/): introduce specs
  gradually and capture the behavior of existing code.
- [Write specs by level](https://specdd.ai/how-to/write-specs-by-level/): choose the scope of a root, module, service,
  feature, policy, or other local spec.
- [Spec-writing techniques](https://specdd.ai/how-to/spec-writing-technique/): turn ideas into useful, maintainable contracts.
- [Use spec sections](https://specdd.ai/how-to/use-spec-sections/): practical guidance for individual sections and notation.
- [Agent workflows](https://specdd.ai/how-to/agent-workflows/): prompt agents, manage context, and review plans.
- [Spec-driven workflows](https://specdd.ai/how-to/spec-driven-workflows/): keep specs and implementation aligned as a
  project changes.
- [Work with SpecDD skills](https://specdd.ai/how-to/work-with-specdd-skills/): choose skills for authoring, planning,
  implementation, review, testing, and other tasks.
- [Testing and quality](https://specdd.ai/how-to/testing-and-quality/): derive checks from specs and identify coverage gaps.
- [Code review and governance](https://specdd.ai/how-to/code-review-and-governance/): review changes against contracts and
  define how specs participate in reviews.
- [Security and risk](https://specdd.ai/how-to/security-and-risk/): document security constraints and assess sensitive changes.
- [Troubleshooting](https://specdd.ai/how-to/troubleshooting/): diagnose setup, syntax, resolution, and agent-behavior problems.

## Perspectives and use cases

The [article collection](https://specdd.ai/articles/) explains the motivation behind SpecDD and explores its use in
different roles and projects.

### Motivation and tradeoffs

- [Why SpecDD was built](https://specdd.ai/articles/i-built-specdd-because-ai-kept-forgetting-what-we-were-building/):
  the origin story and the case for local, persistent project context.
- [Scaling AI-assisted development](https://specdd.ai/articles/scaling-ai-driven-development-needs-a-spec-layer/):
  preserve shared understanding as implementation speed grows and review becomes a bottleneck.
- [Code, specs, and automated tests](https://specdd.ai/articles/the-amazing-trio-code-specs-and-automated-tests/):
  how implementation, intent, and executable checks reinforce each other.
- [The cost and value of writing specs](https://specdd.ai/articles/is-specdd-too-verbose-only-if-you-measure-it-against-toy-code/):
  weigh writing and maintenance effort against repeated clarification, rework, and the lifetime of the code.

### By role

- [SpecDD for developers](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-for-developers/): local context for implementation, refactoring,
  testing, and review.
- [SpecDD for non-technical users](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-for-non-technical-users/): describe behavior,
  constraints, and successful outcomes without designing the implementation.
- [SpecDD for CTOs](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-for-ctos/): engineering intent, architectural control, and review
  quality as AI-assisted development grows.
- [Product and development handoffs](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-as-the-interface-between-product-and-development-teams/):
  use specs as a shared language for requirements and acceptance behavior.
- [SpecDD for DevOps](https://specdd.ai/articles/specdd-for-devops-ansible-roles-and-playbooks/): apply local specs to Ansible
  roles, playbooks, and operational constraints.
